michigan.title: University of Michigan–Ann Arbor
paras: Michigan is a plausible but school-specific transfer target. The Office of Undergraduate Admissions directly reviews College of Literature, Science, and the Arts (LSA) and Engineering applicants; Stamps, Information, Ross, and other units have separate rules. The 2025–26 CDS reports 6,845 Fall 2025 transfer applicants, 2,394 admits, and 1,533 enrollees, a 35.0% university-wide admit rate. It does not reveal the odds for a SCAD student, LSA, a constrained major such as computer science, or an out-of-state applicant. LSA has no minimum number of credits, but says competitive candidates generally present two or more semesters of graded transferable work; the college record carries more weight as an applicant approaches 60 transferable credits. Michigan’s standing deadlines are October 1 for Winter and February 1 for Fall, Spring Half, and Summer Half. The page had not separately labeled a Fall 2027 calendar at the cutoff, so plan for February 1, 2027 and confirm it when the 2026–27 application is live. There is no transfer Early Decision or Early Action round.

Michigan’s 2025–26 CDS marks “level of applicant’s interest” Considered in the first-year C7 table. That is not a transfer scoring rule. Official transfer materials emphasize college performance, transferable quantity and quality, progression, fit with the intended academic area, and high-school work when little college work exists. Treat a Virtual Transfer Spotlight, LSA information session, campus tour, or ambassador conversation as research, not as a points system. The most useful contact question is: “SCAD uses quarter hours and my record includes AI 330 Human in the Loop, AI 360 Systems Design, DIGI 230 Ethics of Emerging Technology, and IDUS 215 Contextual Research. Which of these are likely to count toward LSA distribution, Digital Studies, or Information preparation rather than elective credit, and what syllabus evidence should I submit before planning a four-semester path?” Ask it after checking the transfer-credit equivalency database. Do not email professors to announce an application, and do not send a physical interest package. Michigan highly recommends official documents be transmitted electronically, and transcripts must come from the institution rather than the applicant.

The best liberal-arts bridge is LSA with Digital Studies, Organizational Studies, sociology, psychology, or communication/media, potentially combined with computing or information coursework. The Digital Studies Institute explicitly connects technology with culture, history, identity, and politics. Sophia Brueckner, an associate professor across Stamps, Information, and Digital Studies, combines art, design, engineering, speculative futures, tangible interfaces, algorithms, and the ethics of invention; her Sci-Fi Prototyping work is especially close to SCAD’s design-led AI sequence. Kentaro Toyama, W. K. Kellogg Professor of Community Information, studies technology in international development and social change. These are intellectual anchors, not people to approach for a quick recommendation. A persuasive application would use one completed SCAD project to show that prototyping exposed a deeper question—for example, how an agentic interface redistributes judgment, how a human-in-the-loop workflow encodes institutional power, or how visual explanation changes trust—and then identify the Michigan methods needed to study it.

Research proof: Michigan Medicine independently evaluated the Epic Sepsis Model after it had been deployed broadly with vendor-reported accuracy. Michigan’s responsible-AI account explains that the external validation exposed limits and variation across hospitals rather than assuming a model that worked in one context would generalize everywhere: https://midas.umich.edu/trustworthy-by-design-how-midas-is-shaping-responsible-ai/. That is a concrete model for the applicant’s own “Applied AI plus liberal arts” thesis: design, deployment context, human interpretation, and institutional validation are part of the system, not an afterthought. MIDAS also publishes human-centered AI symposia and public research materials, while Brueckner’s publicly documented prototypes provide a second route into critical design practice.

Michigan has unusually concrete veteran-transfer infrastructure. Most U-M veterans apply as transfers; Veteran & Military Services offers pre-admission guidance, PAVE peer support, and a direct appointment route through program director Philip Larson. LSA’s Transfer Bridges for Military-Connected Students adds pre-transfer academic planning and veteran peer mentorship; eligible military-connected students receive in-state residency, and some may qualify for the Go Blue Guarantee. The summer/fall priority is to enroll in Transfer Bridges, obtain a course-by-course plan, preserve every SCAD syllabus and project brief, and identify an actual instructor who can describe sustained analytical work if a recommendation is later requested. Michigan says an academic evaluator is not required unless requested, so an alumnus or faculty acquaintance created in one month adds no legitimate value. If waitlisted, follow Michigan’s stated restriction: it does not accept extra grades, awards, or a letter of continued interest unless the office asks for them.

Submit official records through the prescribed channel; do not mail a newsletter, promotional portfolio, or “interest” letter, and do not manufacture link activity.

nd.title: University of Notre Dame
paras: Notre Dame’s transfer process is selective, major-specific, and unusually syllabus-intensive. The 2024–25 CDS reports 1,064 Fall 2024 transfer applicants, 267 admits, and 203 enrollees, a 25.1% institutional rate. The current transfer page says recent admitted students average at least a 3.75 college GPA, applicants need one full post-high-school academic year and at least 24 transferable credits, and dual-enrollment credit does not satisfy that minimum. Every applicant selects a college and major; space is particularly limited in Neuroscience and Behavior, Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Business Analytics, and Finance. For this profile, Arts and Letters is more coherent than forcing a capacity-constrained technical major. Notre Dame already posts the next deadlines: Spring 2027 applications are due October 1, 2026, with decisions December 1–January 5; Fall 2027 applications are due March 15, 2027, with decisions May 20–June 14. Transfer applicants do not have ED I, ED II, or Restrictive Early Action.

Notre Dame has said it does not track prospective-student interest. More importantly, the transfer evaluation page tells applicants what actually matters: appropriate prerequisites with grades of B or higher, strong college performance, a strong high-school record, a specific transfer statement, and space in the intended major. A virtual session, campus visit, or conversation with the veteran liaison should answer a real planning question; it should not be a performance. A high-value question is: “Notre Dame requires every post-high-school syllabus. How will the 24-credit eligibility threshold and Arts and Letters prerequisites treat SCAD’s quarter-based Applied AI studios, especially Human in the Loop, Systems Design, Contextual Research, and Ethics of Emerging Technology, and should any be paired with a conventional writing, social-science, or quantitative course before Fall 2027?” The application instructions require a PDF syllabus for every college course, named exactly by course number. A recommendation is optional but encouraged; use a recent instructor who evaluated real work, not an alumnus or admissions contact cultivated in a month.

The academic fit is Arts and Letters plus the Technology and Digital Studies ecosystem, especially the undergraduate Tech Ethics minor. The minor is open across colleges and includes work in AI ethics and governance, algorithms/data/society, race and surveillance, and robot ethics. Mohammad Rashidujjaman Rifat, an assistant professor in computer science and engineering affiliated with HCI, studies AI ethics, cultural and value pluralism, and critical social science approaches to computing. Nitesh Chawla, the Frank M. Freimann Professor of Computer Science and Engineering and founding director of the Lucy Family Institute for Data & Society, works on AI and data science for the common good. Meghan Sullivan, Wilsey Family College Professor of Philosophy and director of the Institute for Ethics and the Common Good, anchors the philosophical side. A credible essay would connect SCAD’s Human in the Loop or Agentic Design work to Notre Dame’s question of the common good: not merely whether a system can be built, but whose capabilities it expands, what obligations it creates, and how it should be governed.

Research proof: the Notre Dame–IBM Technology Ethics Lab’s BenchmarkCards project created a standardized way to document LLM benchmark properties, bias, and evaluation methods, along with a public-access benchmark database; the work also informed IBM watsonx.governance’s Model Risk Evaluation Engine: https://ethics.nd.edu/labs-and-centers/notre-dame-ibm-technology-ethics-lab/collaborative-projects/. The Lab’s broader grants have produced audit frameworks, public tools, and community-centered methods, while its Ethical Cities program brings faculty and students together with South Bend organizations to solve local technology and policy problems: https://ethics.nd.edu/labs-and-centers/notre-dame-ibm-technology-ethics-lab/projects/. This gives the applicant a concrete reason to study Notre Dame: it translates ethics into artifacts, audits, and community implementation—the same bridge SCAD’s design training can support.

Notre Dame’s veteran page explicitly points applicants to Service to School/VetLink and the Warrior-Scholar Project. The Office of Military and Veterans Affairs (OMVA) supports transition and benefits, and the registrar coordinates Yellow Ribbon and VA certification. The best outreach is one note to veteran liaison Montanna Kirven or OMVA describing the educational timeline and asking how SCAD quarter credit, JST/ACE credit, and a veteran’s interruption should be documented. Do not ask the liaison, a professor, or an alumnus for an admissions recommendation; their role is guidance, while a recommender’s role is evidence from sustained work. The optional 60–90 second Glimpse video can show voice and perspective, but it should not repeat the résumé. Official college/high-school transcripts may be mailed by the institution, but a printout of an online application, personal letter, or promotional package should not be mailed. After applying, check the portal repeatedly because missing syllabi keep the file incomplete; if waitlisted, follow the portal’s update instructions rather than starting an email campaign.
actions: Choose an Arts and Letters program and an alternate only after checking each program’s required transfer courses and available space.

Complete a conventional writing-intensive, quantitative-reasoning, or science course if the SCAD record does not clearly cover Notre Dame’s Core preparation.
Request the optional recommendation from a recent academic instructor; use Glimpse only if it adds character and clear spoken reflection.

emory.title: Emory University
paras: Emory admits transfers only for fall. The 2025–26 CDS reports 2,399 Fall 2025 transfer applications, 544 admits, and 173 enrollees, a 22.7% rate. Eligibility requires at least 28 semester hours completed or in progress after high school—AP, IB, and dual-enrollment credits do not satisfy the minimum—and Emory expects at least one full-time year; most successful applicants present a 3.5 or better college GPA. Up to 62 semester hours may transfer, and at least four semesters must be completed at Emory. The current transfer page still displays Fall 2026 dates: March 15 application, March 18 aid, early-May notification, and June 1 deposit. Emory’s general transfer deadline remains March 15, and its aid page already lists March 17, 2027 for Fall 2027 transfer aid; however, the 2027 admission table had not been fully refreshed. Plan for March 15, 2027 and recheck when the application opens in late fall. There is no transfer ED I, ED II, or Early Action, no transfer merit scholarship competition, no interview, and no deferral.

Emory’s 2025–26 CDS marks level of applicant interest Not Considered for first-year applicants. Although that table is not transfer-specific, nothing in the transfer rules supports an email-open or visit-points strategy. The highest-value engagement is a transfer-credit and eligibility check. A precise question is: “Using Emory’s semester conversion, do my SCAD Applied AI and studio courses put me above the 28-credit eligibility floor, and which are likely to satisfy Emory College distribution or the AI minor rather than transfer only as electives? Because my record includes an educational interruption, would the published employer-recommendation exception apply to my exact enrollment dates?” Emory requires one faculty recommendation but permits an employer recommendation when an applicant has been out of college for at least a full year. That is an official contextual option, not a loophole. A new alumnus, professor, or advisor who has only exchanged emails cannot credibly replace someone who supervised or taught the applicant over time.

Emory’s undergraduate AI minor is one of the cleanest curricular bridges in this group. It combines technical study with CS 312 AI, Ethics and Society and electives spanning human-computer interaction, data justice, NLP, sociology, media theory, visualization, rhetoric, and disinformation. Lauren Klein, Winship Distinguished Research Professor of English and Quantitative Methods, directs both the Emory Digital Humanities Lab and the Atlanta Interdisciplinary AI Network; her work on Data Feminism, visualization, and power makes her especially relevant to a designer studying how interfaces make social claims. Joe Sutherland directs the Center for AI Learning, which connects students and faculty with nonprofit, government, corporate, and research partners. The strongest application theme is “from designing intelligent systems to studying the cultures and institutions they organize,” supported by a case study that includes user research, implementation decisions, ethical risks, and what the applicant still cannot answer without Emory’s humanities and social-science methods.

Research proof: Klein and members of the Digital Humanities Lab built Data by Design, a public, interactive research project tracing visualization and power from abolition through the emergence of modern data science; the work is linked from her official Emory profile and is viewable at https://dataxdesign.io/. Emory’s profile describes it as a collaborative book-and-digital project, not a marketing demo: https://english.emory.edu/people/bios/klein-lauren.html. The project matters because it treats charts and interfaces as historical arguments with political effects. It is a direct model for converting a SCAD portfolio from “what I made” into “what the representation authorizes people to believe and do.” The Center for AI Learning also publishes workshops and experiential projects, but access before enrollment should never be assumed; use the public material to refine the application, not to request a pre-admission research role.

Emory says most veteran applicants apply as transfers and provides a named veteran admission liaison, Giles Eady. The registrar coordinates VA certification and Yellow Ribbon, but Yellow Ribbon participation is limited and school-specific rather than an unlimited guarantee, so benefits and remaining cost must be checked in writing. A legitimate summer/fall plan is to complete Service to School’s free advising intake, ask Giles Eady once about veteran documentation and the recommender exception, convert the SCAD transcript, and secure the College Official Report plus a strong faculty letter early. Emory’s page says no other documents are needed or requested beyond the application list, so do not mail a personal letter, newsletter, portfolio, research paper, or promotional package. After applying, verify portal completion and submit aid by March 17, 2027; only send an update through the permitted route if it is genuinely material.
actions: Convert SCAD quarter hours and confirm the 28-semester-hour eligibility floor before doing any outreach.

usc.title: University of Southern California
paras: USC’s Fall 2027 transfer calendar is already explicit. The Common Application opens August 1, 2026. Most majors are due February 15, 2027; selected BFA programs in visual and performing arts are due December 1, 2026; the priority financial-aid deadline is March 2, 2027. By the end of May, applicants receive a decision or a request for spring grades; those asked for spring grades may wait until mid-July. USC’s 2025–26 CDS reports 10,827 Fall 2025 transfer applications, 2,929 admits, and 1,544 enrollees, a 27.1% institutional rate. That figure masks major-level capacity, prerequisite completion, and differences between Dornsife, Annenberg, Viterbi, and the Iovine and Young Academy. USC has no transfer ED, ED II, or Early Action; transfers use one regular process. Applying by the deadline is necessary but does not become a binding signal.

USC states directly that it does not track demonstrated interest and that event attendance, emails, and continued-interest messages do not add admission points: https://www.admissionblog.usc.edu/p/why-we-dont-track-demonstrated-and. Therefore, do not automate link clicks, opens, web sessions, or email replies, and do not send unsolicited award updates. Use official events and advising to make the major choice. The highest-value question is for the Iovine and Young Academy: “With SCAD’s Applied AI foundation, Human in the Loop, Systems Design, and three-studio sequence, which Academy requirements are structurally non-waivable for an external transfer, and should I realistically budget three or four USC years in the BS Innovation Design and Technology or BS Human Technology Interaction path?” This cannot be answered by a generic brochure because it depends on the transcript and sequential curriculum. Ask once at iyaadmission@usc.edu with a one-page course list; do not ask a faculty member for a pre-review or recommendation.

The Iovine and Young Academy is the closest direct fit because it integrates design, technology, entrepreneurship, and human-centered problem solving, but its sequential curriculum can extend time-to-degree. Annenberg communication or Dornsife sociology/media is the stronger liberal-arts alternative; Viterbi is appropriate only if calculus, programming, science, and technical prerequisites are genuinely complete. Kate Crawford, research professor of communication and science and technology studies at USC Annenberg, studies the power, labor, environmental cost, and politics of AI; her visual investigation Anatomy of an AI System maps the Amazon Echo’s full material and data lifecycle. Bistra Dilkina, associate professor of computer science and co-director of the Center for AI in Society, teaches undergraduate AI for Social Good and works on computational methods for social and environmental problems. The application should choose one pathway and explain why its structure—not USC’s general reputation—is required to turn the applicant’s design practice into accountable research and implementation.

Research proof: USC’s Center for AI in Society and social-work partners ran an AI-assisted network intervention with youth experiencing homelessness that produced a reported 40% increase in HIV testing; USC describes the pilot and its community context here: https://computing.usc.edu/uscs-leadership-in-tech-innovation/. The center later completed a three-year collaboration with the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority and UCLA’s California Policy Lab to identify racial bias in housing triage and develop a fairer decision-support approach with a community advisory board: https://today.usc.edu/artificial-intelligence-could-reduce-racial-bias-in-homeless-services-usc-scientists-say/. These are not abstract “AI for good” claims: they are implemented, evaluated interventions that combine technical design, social work, trauma-aware research, and public policy. They provide a clear model for how a SCAD project could mature at USC.

USC’s Veterans Resource Center supports military-affiliated students with transition, leadership, career, and benefits programming; the Veterans Certification Office handles Chapter 33, VR&E, and Yellow Ribbon processes. USC reports an unlimited undergraduate Yellow Ribbon program for eligible students at the 100% Post-9/11 level, but the applicant should still obtain a written net-cost and time-to-degree estimate because extra sequential semesters change living costs and benefit usage. A veteran fee waiver is available in the transfer application. Use Service to School for application mentorship, then contact the VRC for transition/benefits—not for an admissions endorsement. Portfolios should be submitted only when the target program invites or requires them, and should show validated design process, user research, iteration, and results rather than decorative work. Do not mail a creative package; official transcripts and portfolio files belong in USC’s stated systems. Post-application, respond promptly to a spring-grade request and avoid a continued-interest email unless USC explicitly creates a form for that situation.
actions: By August, choose among Iovine and Young, Annenberg/Dornsife, and Viterbi based on prerequisites, transfer credit, and remaining semesters—not prestige.
Use USC’s transfer planning worksheet and articulation resources, then ask Iovine and Young the sequencing question above if that is the chosen route.
Build one portfolio case study around problem framing, contextual research, prototype, human-in-loop decisions, testing, and measurable learning.
Obtain an academic recommendation only if the target school/program requests or permits it; do not substitute an alumnus or faculty cold contact.
File the Common App after August 1 and before the correct December 1 or February 15 deadline; complete aid by March 2, 2027.
Secure a written VA/Yellow Ribbon and time-to-degree estimate before committing, especially for a three- or four-year Academy sequence.

vandy.title: Vanderbilt University
paras: Vanderbilt is a plausible but highly selective transfer target whose best argument is academic coherence, not engagement volume. Its 2025–26 Common Data Set reports 3,177 transfer applicants, 831 admits, and 446 enrollees, an admit rate of about 26.2%. That aggregate is not a personal probability: review is conducted in the context of the undergraduate school and available space, and the record must show that the applicant can enter the intended curriculum without losing academic momentum. Vanderbilt says it usually enrolls roughly 450 transfer students each fall, requires at least four semesters in residence, and gives preference to applicants whose recent path shows sustained full-time engagement in a rigorous collegiate setting, while reviewing interruptions in context. A veteran or nontraditional applicant should therefore explain service, work, and any enrollment gaps plainly, then make recent graded college work the primary proof of readiness.

Vanderbilt’s standing transfer priority deadline is February 15, with applications considered on a rolling basis afterward only while space remains; the university says it usually stops accepting transfer applications by May 1. As of July 17, 2026, the transfer page does not separately label a Fall 2027 calendar, so February 15, 2027 is the prudent planning date but must be rechecked when the next cycle is posted. There is no transfer Early Decision, ED II, Early Action, or binding transfer round. Two academic teacher recommendations are required, and Vanderbilt strongly prefers that at least one come from a college instructor. The 2025–26 Common Data Set’s first-year table marks “level of applicant’s interest” as not considered; that table is not a transfer-factor table, but Vanderbilt’s transfer instructions likewise provide no basis for treating email opens, visits, or faculty contacts as admission points. The useful contact is one concise clarification tied to curricular planning, not repeated outreach.

The strongest SCAD Applied AI bridge is a liberal-arts field that studies technology in society, reinforced by quantitative and design coursework. Vanderbilt’s Data Science minor includes pathways involving AI, material culture, visualization, and society, while the new Innovation and Design Strategy minor is intended to expand cross-disciplinary, hands-on learning. Sociology professor Jenny L. Davis studies the politics and ethics of technological design and algorithmic systems; computer science professor Jules White works on generative AI and its practical use; and mechanical engineering/computer science professor Nilanjan Sarkar studies human–robot interaction, affective computing, and virtual environments. Those are intellectual anchors for a “human systems and responsible AI” story, not people to cultivate for an admission recommendation. A precise, answerable question for transfer admissions is: “How would quarter-based SCAD courses such as Contextual Research, Ethics of Emerging Technology, Human in the Loop, Systems Design, and sequential Applied AI studios be evaluated for Arts and Science preparation versus unrestricted elective credit, and what syllabus evidence would help the evaluator?”

Research proof: Vanderbilt’s Smart Cities work shows how computation, design, and public systems become an implemented civic project. In partnership with Nashville, researchers have worked on transit tools associated with WeGo and, through a 2022 NSF Civic Innovation Challenge project, explored an AI-supported system for routing appropriate non-emergency incidents away from overburdened emergency response. The point is not merely that Vanderbilt “does AI”; the work asks how a technical intervention enters a real municipal workflow and affects residents, dispatchers, and scarce public resources. An applicant could study this work and propose a future inquiry about participatory interface design, error escalation, or public accountability—an unusually credible connection to SCAD’s human-in-loop and systems-design foundation. Vanderbilt’s VALIANT AI Summer School is another current learning venue; its August 10–14, 2026 program is advertised to the wider Middle Tennessee AI ecosystem, but cost and public eligibility should be confirmed rather than assumed.

Veteran strategy must include benefits math. Vanderbilt’s registrar certifies VA educational benefits, and eligible students may use Yellow Ribbon; the university’s current page describes school-specific annual contribution limits, so obtain a written estimate from the VA School Certifying Official rather than extrapolating from a headline. Service to School can improve application structure and school selection, but it cannot supply the required academic recommendations. An alumnus, admissions adviser, or professor met through one conversation should not be asked for a letter: such a letter cannot replace the required instructor evaluations and would reveal little direct knowledge of the applicant’s work. Do not mail a résumé, research paper, portfolio, or “interest” letter unless Vanderbilt asks for it. After applying, use the portal for requested materials and semester grades, and send an update only if Vanderbilt’s instructions permit it and the update is genuinely material.
actions: Choose the intended Vanderbilt undergraduate school and audit its prerequisites and four-semester residency requirement against a realistic credit evaluation.

Treat February 15, 2027 as the working deadline, submit well before it, and recheck the published Fall 2027 calendar when it appears.
Obtain a written Yellow Ribbon, GI Bill, housing, and time-to-degree estimate before choosing Vanderbilt over a public in-state option.

columbia.title: Columbia University School of General Studies
paras: Columbia GS is structurally different from a conventional transfer pathway and may be the strongest nontraditional fit in this group. It was created for students whose education has been interrupted for at least a year or who have a compelling reason to attend part time, and it allows full- or part-time enrollment in Columbia’s undergraduate liberal-arts curriculum. More than three-quarters of entering GS students bring transfer credit. The GS-specific 2024–25 Common Data Set reports 1,330 transfer applications, 697 admits, and 410 enrollees, an admit rate of about 52.4%; Columbia’s institutional summary separately reports 414 fall transfer enrollees, so use the standardized CDS figure for rate calculations and recognize the small reporting difference. That rate does not make GS a safety. Columbia says recent college students are generally expected to present approximately A-level work, commonly a 3.7–3.8 record, and the autobiographical essay must explain the interruption, the return to school, and the intellectual direction with unusual clarity.

GS has its own rolling calendar and its “early” options are not Early Decision. For Fall 2027, the application opens December 1, 2026; the priority Early Action deadline is January 15, the later Early Action deadline is March 1, and Regular Decision is May 15. For Spring 2027, the application opens August 1, 2026, with priority Early Action September 1, Early Action October 1, and Regular Decision November 1. GS describes decisions as generally arriving six to eight weeks after a completed application, and its Early Action plans are nonbinding. There is no transfer ED I or ED II, so the claimed “mathematical advantage” of binding ED does not apply. The GS CDS marks applicant interest “very important” in its first-time first-year C7 table, but the transfer section supplies no analogous factor table. A prompt, well-researched application and a legitimate advising appointment can clarify fit; there is no official basis for automated opens, clicks, repeated mailing-list registrations, or manufactured contact as a transfer-selection strategy.

The academic case can be both technical and humanistic. Columbia now offers an undergraduate major in Artificial Intelligence through GS, while Sociology’s AI work examines how algorithmic systems reorganize institutions, labor, culture, and inequality. Associate professor Dan J. Wang studies technology, organizations, innovation, and careers; sociologist Gil Eyal teaches and writes about expertise, knowledge, and AI in society. The applicant could also consider sociology, urban studies, visual arts, or information-oriented coursework alongside computing rather than assuming every SCAD course will map neatly into the AI major. GS may accept up to 60 credits of liberal-arts work graded C or better, but every student must complete at least 64 Columbia points. A high-value advising question is: “Given my exact break-in-enrollment timeline and SCAD’s quarter curriculum, which Applied AI studios and courses in design thinking, contextual research, systems design, and ethics are likely to be liberal-arts transfer credit, which could satisfy prerequisites, and which would remain elective only—and what would a full-time versus part-time path cost?”

Research proof: Columbia’s Center for Spatial Research created Million Dollar Blocks by combining and mapping criminal-justice data to show where state spending on incarceration is concentrated at the city-block level. The public project covers multiple U.S. cities and turns otherwise inaccessible administrative data into visual evidence that community organizations and policy partners can interrogate. It matters for this applicant because the work is simultaneously data analysis, information design, sociology, and public communication: it asks not only whether a map is technically accurate, but what institutional choices it makes visible and who can act on it. A credible application connection would analyze one visualization choice or propose a community-governed extension—not merely name the project. Columbia’s Artificial Intelligence for Social Good and Society initiative offers a second relevant model through projects such as overdose-risk analysis and community-facing data tools.

GS is also unusually experienced with veterans. Its veterans pages report a community of more than 300 student veterans and state that veterans represented roughly 24% of the Fall 2025 entering class; the Columbia Veterans Transition Initiative and campus veteran organizations add transition and peer support. The crucial constraint is cost: GS financial aid is administered separately from Columbia College, does not promise to meet every student’s full demonstrated need, and part-time/full-time choices affect aid and benefits. Get a written estimate covering accepted credits, remaining Columbia points, tuition, housing, Post-9/11 GI Bill, and current Yellow Ribbon participation before choosing an entry term. The application asks for two academic or professional recommendations, so a long-term supervisor may be appropriate when that person has directly evaluated the applicant. An admissions officer, alumnus, or professor encountered through one month of networking is not a credible substitute. Do not mail a personal package; submit transcripts and any requested official record through the prescribed channel, and use an optional interview only to explain the record rather than perform enthusiasm.
actions: Ask GS admissions to confirm nontraditional eligibility from the exact enrollment and service timeline before investing in the application.
Book one advising appointment to review transfer-credit categories, the 64-point residency minimum, AI-major prerequisites, and full-time versus part-time cost.
Build the 1,500–2,000-word autobiographical essay around cause-and-effect: interruption, service/work growth, return to academic rigor, SCAD Applied AI, and the next intellectual problem.
Select two recommenders with sustained direct knowledge—recent faculty where possible and a substantive military or professional supervisor where appropriate.
If applying for Fall 2027, target the January 15 priority Early Action deadline; do not describe it as binding or as ED.
Before enrollment, obtain written financial-aid and VA-benefits scenarios for several transfer-credit outcomes and both enrollment intensities.

washu.title: Washington University in St. Louis
paras: WashU is a high-reach transfer option, and the intended undergraduate division matters. Its 2024–25 Common Data Set reports 1,706 transfer applicants, 239 admits, and 99 enrollees, an admit rate of about 14.0%. The university says admission depends on space and the applicant’s preparation for the chosen school; students enter one division and ordinarily remain there for at least their first semester. Applicants who have been away from formal education for more than two years are encouraged to show roughly 30 units of recent work within a year, and every transfer must complete at least four consecutive full-time semesters at WashU. Those rules make recent rigor and a realistic degree map far more persuasive than a campaign of contacts. A veteran/nontraditional applicant should use the additional-information section to explain service or interruption without allowing the explanation to replace evidence from current college coursework.

WashU’s current quick-view admissions page lists March 1 as the fall-transfer deadline, while a detailed transfer table still carries the previous cycle’s date labeling and shows early-March processing. As of July 17, 2026, a fully relabeled Fall 2027 transfer table has not been posted, so March 1, 2027 is the safe working deadline and must be verified after the application calendar refreshes. Spring transfer admission uses an October deadline when offered. Transfers do not apply through ED I, ED II, or Early Decision; those rounds belong to first-year admission. WashU has announced that it will consider demonstrated interest beginning with Fall 2027 high-school applicants, naming official visits, virtual programs, school visits, college fairs, and Bear Chats. That announcement does not say the new policy applies to transfer review. Therefore, do not assume it does: ask the transfer office once, “Does the Fall 2027 demonstrated-interest policy apply to transfer applicants, and if so, which registered activities are actually included?” Until WashU answers, record attendance for personal learning but assign it no admission points.

The required application evidence is concrete: the transfer application, all college and high-school records, the College Report, and an instructor evaluation; art applicants need a portfolio, and architecture applicants are encouraged to submit one. The applicant should choose a division before building the narrative. Sam Fox offers a BA in Design and coursework in creative computation, AI and art, and human–computer interaction; Arts & Sciences provides humanities and social-science routes; and the university’s new 15-credit minor in computational artificial intelligence, directed by Chongjie Zhang and beginning in Fall 2026, is designed to be available across undergraduate schools. The Data Science BS also includes human-centered design, responsible data science, and AI-and-society options. A SCAD-to-WashU story could therefore join design practice with sociology, digital humanities, or responsible computation rather than present Applied AI as a duplicate of computer science.

Named intellectual matches include Alvitta Ottley, whose computer science research examines personalized and adaptive visualization, decision-making, and human–computer interaction, and Gabrielle “Gabi” Kirilloff, whose digital-humanities work uses computational methods to study literature and culture. Contact them only after reading an actual project or publication, and ask a narrow scholarly question—not for admission guidance, an informal review, or a future recommendation. The more important institutional question is for transfer admissions or the chosen division: “How will SCAD’s quarter courses in Contextual Research, Ethics of Emerging Technology, Human in the Loop, Systems Design, and Applied AI studio be converted, and which could satisfy distribution, major, HCI, or new AI-minor requirements rather than elective credit?” A syllabus packet can be prepared in advance, but should be sent only if the evaluator asks for it.

Research proof: WashU’s Humanities Digital Workshop and Program in Digital Transformation support “AI Style,” a project by Gabi Kirilloff, Claudia Carroll, and collaborators that uses computational stylometry and humanistic interpretation to test how generative models imitate nineteenth-century literary style. Its public project description and related scholarly work make the research inspectable: investigators are not simply celebrating an LLM output, but comparing patterns, authorship, genre, and the limitations of machine-produced imitation. It matters because it connects model evaluation to cultural history and asks what a quantitative similarity measure misses—an ideal bridge between SCAD’s algorithm design, contextual research, and design ethics. A strong application could explain a small replication or critique using design artifacts or another cultural corpus. WashU’s Digital Transformation Research Corps also sponsors implemented local-facing projects, including cultural-asset mapping in St. Louis, which offers a second route into participatory design and community data.

WashU’s Office of Military and Veteran Services supports benefit navigation, transition, and community, while the registrar certifies VA benefits. The applicant should request current Yellow Ribbon and net-price details directly because eligibility, school contribution, transfer credits, and time to degree interact. Service to School may supply a mentor and application review, but neither S2S nor a newly met alumnus can replace the instructor evaluation or College Report. Do not manufacture a month-long relationship for a letter; readers value first-hand evidence of academic behavior. Do not mail a portfolio or “interest” note outside the stated submission process. After application, submit requested grades or documents through the portal and communicate only a material update that the office says it will accept.
actions: Pick the WashU undergraduate division, then build a four-semester-plus degree map under several transfer-credit outcomes.
Ask transfer admissions whether Fall 2027 interest tracking applies to transfers and record the answer; do not automate engagement.
Confirm how SCAD quarter credit and the Applied AI studio sequence would map to the intended major and the new computational AI minor.
Secure the required instructor evaluation from someone who has directly graded substantial work; request the College Report early.
Create a research note on AI Style or a St. Louis Digital Transformation project and use it only where it genuinely explains intellectual fit.
Work toward March 1, 2027, then verify the official Fall 2027 calendar as soon as WashU relabels the cycle.

uva.title: University of Virginia
paras: UVA is a selective transfer target with a pronounced residency and pathway context. Its 2024–25 Common Data Set reports 4,245 transfer applications, 1,357 admits, and 851 enrollees, an admit rate of about 32.0%. UVA’s own transfer-admission blog reports a larger Fall 2025 pool of 4,665 applications and approximate offer rates of 33% for Virginia residents and 17% for out-of-state applicants; it also reports variation by school, from roughly 12% for Commerce and 14% for Architecture to 26% for Arts & Sciences and 27% for Engineering. Those newer figures are an operational admissions-office blog, not yet the standardized 2025–26 CDS, and should be labeled accordingly. They show why the aggregate admit rate is not a personal chance. The applicant needs at least 24 transferable semester hours completed or in progress, must ordinarily be at least one year removed from high school, and must complete at least four semesters in residence.

Fall transfer applications are due March 1 with decisions by May 1; Spring transfer applications are due October 1 with decisions by December 1, but spring admission is limited to the College of Arts & Sciences and space is tight. UVA has no transfer ED I, ED II, Early Action, or binding round. The university explicitly says it does not track demonstrated interest. Its transfer instructions also tell applicants not to send résumés, research papers, or extra items, apart from a qualified arts portfolio in the relevant circumstance; application updates belong in the applicant portal rather than duplicated by email. That removes a great deal of false work: a tour, webinar, or thoughtful email can improve the applicant’s judgment and essay, but it does not earn a telemetry score. Do not automate opens or clicks, and do not mail a “creative” admissions packet.

Academic route selection is especially important because UVA’s Bachelor of Science in Data Science does not admit external transfer students. An applicant interested in Applied AI should not build a plan around transferring directly into that degree. A more realistic route could be the College of Arts & Sciences in Media Studies, Sociology, Psychology, or another liberal-arts field, combined—if prerequisites, credit, and capacity permit—with the five-course Data Science minor. This would preserve the strongest parts of the SCAD background: contextual research, design thinking, ethical technology, visual communication, and human-in-loop systems. Mona Sloane, an associate professor of data science and media studies, is a particularly relevant scholar: her work examines the design, use, and governance of AI through sociology, policy, and participatory research. She is an intellectual reference, not a route around admission.

Research proof: a 2026 UVA Data Science and Environmental Institute CoLab project, “Community Climate Knowledge and Multimodal Climate AI,” is integrating community-generated knowledge into multimodal climate models while examining equitable data governance. The project runs through June 2028 and treats local knowledge and community participation as part of the model-building process, rather than data to be extracted after technical choices are fixed. It offers a concrete bridge from SCAD’s contextual research and human-in-loop studios to a consequential public problem: how interfaces, consent, provenance, and institutional power shape the usefulness of climate AI. The Sloane Lab’s public “Co-Opting AI” virtual series and recordings provide an accessible summer/fall study resource; an applicant could write a brief critical response or small prototype, but should not contact a professor simply to announce attendance.

The best pre-application question is administrative and highly specific: “Because the external-transfer BS in Data Science is closed, can an Arts & Sciences transfer realistically complete Media Studies or Sociology plus the Data Science minor within UVA’s residency rules after conversion of my SCAD quarter credits, and which Applied AI studios would count only as electives?” Direct the credit-policy portion to admissions/transfer advising rather than asking a professor to pre-evaluate the transcript. UVA permits an optional recommendation, but optional does not mean “find a famous person.” If used, it should come from a recent professor or supervisor who can provide first-hand evidence of academic readiness, writing, collaboration, and mature judgment. An alumnus met for a month, an admissions counselor, or a faculty member who answered one question has no basis for a useful letter and should not be asked.

UVA’s Veterans Student Center, Student Veterans of America community, and Warrior-Scholar programming can support transition. The current Yellow Ribbon page is unusually important for an out-of-state veteran: it lists only five undergraduate recipients and a maximum institutional contribution of $1,000, awarded on a first-come basis; the VA match is separate, and the public-university GI Bill rules differ for in-state tuition. Confirm the coming year’s terms, residency eligibility, benefit tier, and expected transfer credit in writing before treating UVA as affordable. Service to School is useful for narrative, application review, and veteran-to-veteran mentorship, but it does not change UVA’s course prerequisites or supply an admissions endorsement. Post-application, monitor the portal, send only requested midterm/official records, and do not invent a LOCI unless the office asks for one.
actions: Eliminate the external-transfer BS in Data Science from the plan and select a viable College of Arts & Sciences major before drafting the application.
Use UVA’s transfer-course and school requirements to map at least 24 transferable semester hours and four remaining semesters.
Ask the single route-and-credit question above; do not attach a portfolio, résumé, research paper, or unsolicited syllabus packet.
Study the community-climate-AI project and one Co-Opting AI session, then connect a specific methodological insight to existing SCAD work.
If submitting the optional recommendation, choose a person with sustained direct knowledge and give that person the UVA academic argument and deadlines.
Submit by March 1, 2027 for fall, then use only the portal for permitted updates; confirm veteran benefits and residency before enrollment.

cornell.title: Cornell University
paras: Cornell has one conventional transfer route, organized by the undergraduate college or school to which the applicant applies. The current transfer page lists a March 15 deadline for the Common Application, Cornell questions and writing supplement, fee or waiver, high-school and college transcripts, College Report, a college-instructor academic recommendation, Mid-Term Report, aid materials, and any college-specific supplement; supporting materials have an April 15 final deadline. Decisions are released weekly from late April through June, and admitted students normally receive 30 days to reply. Cornell’s 2025–26 CDS reports 7,381 Fall 2025 transfer applicants, 864 admits, and 625 enrollees, a 11.7% admit rate. That is useful scale, but the applicant’s target college, prerequisite preparation, available space, credit map, grades, and reason for transferring matter more than the university-wide percentage. Cornell offers no transfer ED I or ED II; the November 1 Early Decision route is for first-year applicants. Cornell had not separately posted a Fall 2027 transfer opening date at this research cutoff, so March 15 should be treated as the current standing deadline and rechecked when the next Common App cycle opens.

Cornell’s current CDS marks “level of applicant’s interest” Not Considered for first-year admission, and Cornell publishes no transfer-specific interest score. The productive goal is therefore not to accumulate clicks, opens, mailings, or repeated emails. The productive goal is to learn which Cornell college fits, complete its required transfer coursework, and write a precise college-specific explanation. Attend one official transfer or college session if it answers a real planning need, keep one identity and email address so records match, and send at most one well-researched question to admissions or the relevant college. A worthwhile question is: “For an applicant transferring from SCAD’s Applied AI curriculum into the College of Arts and Sciences Information Science major, which programming, calculus, statistics, and social-science courses normally satisfy entry preparation, and which are typically awarded only elective credit?” A mailed letter, gift, newsletter, or faculty introduction has no documented admissions value; official records should be sent through the requested electronic channel unless Cornell instructs otherwise.

The strongest intellectual bridge is Information Science, available through Arts and Sciences and CALS, because it combines computation with Behavioral Science, Interactive Technologies, Networks/Crowds/Markets, and UX-oriented study. Claire Cardie, the John C. Ford Professor of Engineering, works in natural-language processing, argumentation, deception, and human-centered NLP. Allison Koenecke studies algorithmic fairness, including speech-recognition disparities and the effects of automated systems in public benefits and health. René Kizilcec directs the Future of Learning Lab and connects education technology, computational social science, ethics, and human-computer interaction. Those names are research anchors, not prospective recommenders. A strong Cornell essay would take one finished SCAD project, identify its design and social stakes, and explain which Cornell methods would allow the applicant to evaluate the system rather than merely build it. Before naming any professor, read one current project or paper and connect it to a concrete question already present in the applicant’s work.

Cornell has a dedicated veteran admissions pathway and states that document waivers or substitutions may be possible for military applicants whose circumstances make standard documents unavailable. It also offers a Veterans Summer Bridge, a veteran community, Yellow Ribbon participation, and need-based aid intended to meet full demonstrated need for eligible undergraduates. The most credible summer/fall work is to obtain a college-by-college transfer-credit review where available, save full SCAD syllabi and project briefs, complete a rigorous writing or quantitative course if there is a prerequisite gap, obtain an academic recommendation from an instructor who evaluated substantial work, and develop a compact portfolio or research memo only if the receiving college permits it. A commanding officer or supervisor can add context when Cornell permits an extra letter, but cannot replace the required college-instructor recommendation merely because a relationship is impressive. After applying, monitor the portal, submit the Mid-Term Report and aid documents on time, and report only material academic or professional updates.

One concrete Cornell research asset is the Future of Learning Lab’s field study of 1.4 million registrations across 159 online courses at 20 institutions. The team coded 40 visual and verbal features on Stanford Online and edX enrollment pages and found that course discipline, stated prerequisites, and gender cues predicted who enrolled, while instructor skin color, diversity references, and the linguistic style of descriptions did not show the expected effects. The finding matters for an Applied AI/design applicant because it demonstrates a rigorous way to test interface and messaging assumptions at scale rather than treating inclusive design as surface styling. It also supplies an honest intellectual entry point for a portfolio case study: formulate a behavioral claim, identify measurable interface features, test it with real usage data, and discuss where correlation does and does not justify design intervention.
actions: Choose the Cornell undergraduate college first and audit every college-specific prerequisite against SCAD transcripts and syllabi.
By early fall, ask a recent SCAD instructor who graded analytical or technical work for the required academic recommendation.
Attend one official transfer/college event and ask the transfer-credit or preparation question above if the published materials do not resolve it.
Build the essay around one Applied AI project, its human consequences, and a specific Cornell method, concentration, lab, or course sequence.
Prepare the Common App, Cornell supplement, College Report, Mid-Term Report, transcripts, aid forms, and any permitted portfolio well before the standing March 15 deadline.
Do not automate email opens/clicks, mass-contact faculty, mail promotional packages, or seek a recommendation from someone who knows the applicant only through a recent cold email.

northeastern.title: Northeastern University
paras: Northeastern admits transfers for both fall and spring. Its current deadline page lists April 15 for fall transfer admission, with rolling decisions released no later than June 30, and October 15 for spring, with decisions no later than December 15; the associated FAFSA/CSS deadlines are the same. Northeastern generally treats a student as a transfer applicant after 12 semester hours earned after high school or one attempted full-time college semester with continued enrollment. The latest official CDS posted at the research cutoff is 2024–25: 3,420 Fall 2024 transfer applicants, 675 admits, and 288 enrollees, a 19.7% admit rate. It does not reveal outcomes by college, major, campus, or credit profile. Northeastern does not offer transfer ED I or ED II; its ED rounds are first-year plans, while transfers use the regular rolling process. The published deadline page should be rechecked when the 2026–27 application is live because Northeastern had not labeled these dates “Fall 2027” at the cutoff.

The CDS marks level of applicant interest Considered for first-year applicants, but Northeastern publishes no transfer-specific demonstrated-interest rating. Its counselor resources encourage visits, engagement, and questions, yet that is not evidence that a transfer applicant receives points for email behavior. The legitimate use of engagement is to learn how the combined-major curriculum, transfer-credit evaluation, campus placement, and co-op sequence work. A high-value question is: “For a transfer entering AI and Philosophy or Computer Science and Design with SCAD Applied AI and studio coursework, which credits can satisfy both sides of the combined major, and how would the remaining sequence affect the earliest eligible co-op term?” Send it once through the official transfer contact route after reviewing the catalog. Do not create automated opens, clicks, webinar attendance, or reply sequences; fabricated activity is not academic evidence and can create an incoherent contact record.

Northeastern offers unusually direct curricular combinations for this profile. The BS in Artificial Intelligence and Philosophy joins AI, logic, ethics, privacy, and social analysis; the BS in Computer Science and Design joins computation with interaction and visual design. Dakuo Wang, jointly appointed in Khoury College and the College of Arts, Media and Design, researches human–AI collaboration and human-centered AI. Upol Ehsan works in human-centered explainable AI, responsible AI, and participatory civic AI. Kathleen “Katie” Creel is jointly appointed in computer science and social sciences/humanities and studies algorithmic fairness, transparency, explanation, and AI monoculture. These faculty make a coherent research triangle for an applicant who can show how SCAD design practice led to questions about explanation, power, and collaboration. A serious “Why transfer” statement should also explain why Northeastern’s co-op and experiential structure is necessary for the next stage of the work, not simply praise Boston or rankings.

The Center for the Advancement of Veterans and Servicemembers (CAVS) coordinates military support, and Northeastern states that eligible undergraduates at the 100% Post-9/11 GI Bill level are automatically included in its unlimited Yellow Ribbon program. The transfer plan should therefore integrate credit, time-to-degree, co-op timing, and VA certification before treating Northeastern as affordable. Summer and fall priorities are to request a preliminary credit map, preserve syllabi and project documentation, identify one recent academic recommender, and turn an Applied AI project into a short case study showing problem definition, user research, technical choices, ethical tradeoffs, and measurable results. After applying, check the portal for missing items and complete financial-aid and benefit certification promptly. Contacting faculty is appropriate only for a precise scholarly question after reading their work; a one-month email acquaintance is not a legitimate substitute for an instructor or supervisor recommendation.

Northeastern’s StoryMate is a useful implemented research asset, not merely a proposed lab theme. Dakuo Wang’s team worked with kindergarten teachers to annotate 200 children’s stories with realistic questions and answers, used those annotations to build an open-source conversational-reading system, then tested it with children, parents, and teachers. The university reports that children generally liked it, parents said it helped them ask better questions, and teachers saw sustained reading engagement; in summer 2025 the team began a larger classroom test in two California school districts serving many Spanish-speaking families. The project matters because it connects participatory design, expert annotation, LLM behavior, literacy, and field evaluation—the exact bridge between design and social science that a strong SCAD-to-Northeastern application should make.
actions: Compare AI and Philosophy with Computer Science and Design course by course, including co-op prerequisites and anticipated transfer credit.
Attend one official transfer information session; use it to clarify credit, campus, and co-op sequencing rather than to create an attendance count.
Ask the combined-major/first-co-op question once if the catalog and transfer session leave it unresolved.
Build one portfolio case study that connects design craft, AI implementation, responsible evaluation, and user impact.
Submit early enough for a complete rolling review, but do not confuse early completion with a binding or separately advantaged transfer round.
Before enrollment, obtain a written cost and VA-benefit estimate from CAVS and financial aid.

yale.title: Yale University — Eli Whitney Students Program
paras: The Eli Whitney Students Program (EWSP) is Yale College’s nontraditional route to the same BA or BS, with full- or part-time enrollment. Eligibility generally requires either a five-year interruption in postsecondary education or being at least five years beyond high-school graduation by matriculation; applicants may not already hold a bachelor’s degree. Yale’s transfer Common Application for EWSP opens in late November, the application deadline is March 1 for fall entry, supporting materials are due March 15, and financial-aid materials are due April 1. A small group is invited to virtual interviews in April or May, with decisions in mid-May. Yale’s 2025–26 CDS reports 1,747 Fall 2025 transfer applicants, 45 admits, and 35 enrollees, a 2.6% overall transfer rate, but it does not break out EWSP; that percentage must not be presented as an EWSP acceptance rate. There is no EWSP transfer ED or Yale Single-Choice Early Action route. A veteran should compare EWSP with the conventional transfer pathway and apply through only one Yale College route.

Yale states directly that it does not track event registrations or contact with admissions staff for evaluation. There is therefore no legitimate advantage in manufactured opens, link clicks, repeated inquiries, mailed letters, or attempts to get a counselor to “put in a word.” Engagement is useful only for resolving pathway, eligibility, credit, and academic-planning questions. A focused question for EWSP is: “Given my exact military/educational timeline and SCAD Applied AI record, should I use EWSP rather than conventional transfer, and how are studio-based computing courses evaluated toward Computing and the Arts prerequisites versus elective credit?” Send the timeline and question concisely to the EWSP office after reviewing the eligibility page. Yale permits two recommendations and prefers recent academic voices, but EWSP explicitly allows employers, mentors, or colleagues when an applicant has not recently been enrolled; an additional nonacademic letter may provide context. That flexibility is not a loophole: the writer must have observed sustained, substantive work.

Yale’s Computing and the Arts major is a particularly close academic match because it joins computing with art, architecture, history of art, music, or theater and culminates in a jointly supervised senior project. Marynel Vázquez, an assistant professor of computer science, studies human–robot interaction, social AI, and how systems infer and respond to social behavior. Theodore Kim, a professor of computer science associated with the Critical Computing Initiative, connects computer graphics to the field’s history, representation, and racial bias. Those resources support an intellectually stronger application theme than “I want elite AI”: the applicant can argue that design decisions are social decisions, and that moving from SCAD’s applied practice into Yale’s liberal-arts environment would enable historical, ethical, and empirical analysis of those decisions. A strong graded analytical paper or writing sample should demonstrate current readiness for Yale’s reading and writing intensity.

Yale’s veteran guidance says strong recent college work in reading/writing, quantitative reasoning, social sciences, humanities, and science is valuable; veterans receive an automatic application-fee waiver. The university also provides a veteran and military student office, need-based aid, and a pathway for VA benefit coordination. Summer/fall work should prioritize recent rigorous coursework if the transcript is old or uneven, a concise educational-interruption narrative, one polished academic paper, exact syllabus collection, and early recommender conversations. Use the additional-information section to explain the timeline and responsibilities without turning the entire application into a résumé. After submission, monitor the portal, complete aid by April 1, prepare for a possible interview, and send only genuinely new academic, professional, or service developments. Do not mail creative packages or solicit faculty advocacy; neither substitutes for the required academic case.

Yale’s Anti-Racist Graphics initiative is a concrete research program with direct relevance to a design-trained applicant. Theodore Kim and collaborators documented how graphics research and commercial rendering had treated the optical behavior of lighter skin and straighter hair as a supposedly universal human default; the group then developed counterexamples and new technical formulations, including the 2023 “Lifted Curls” model for tightly coiled hair, which won a best-paper award at the Symposium on Computer Animation. This matters because the work does more than critique representation after an image is made: it traces cultural bias into data, physical assumptions, rendering algorithms, and evaluation standards. A SCAD project could be discussed at that same technical-and-humanistic level without claiming any relationship to the lab.
actions: Email EWSP once with the exact dates of high-school graduation, every college enrollment, service, and interruption to confirm the proper Yale pathway.
Audit recent coursework across writing, quantitative reasoning, humanities/social science, and science; address the clearest readiness gap during fall if feasible.
Select two recommenders who have directly evaluated sustained work; use EWSP’s nonacademic flexibility only when necessary and evidence-based.
Develop a Computing and the Arts rationale around one SCAD project and one social, historical, or ethical question it exposed.
Prepare the application for the late-November opening and March 1 deadline, with materials by March 15 and aid by April 1.
Treat an interview invitation as selective, prepare specific Yale questions, and do not read the absence of an invitation as an instruction to lobby.

brown.title: Brown University — Resumed Undergraduate Education and Veterans Application
paras: Brown’s Resumed Undergraduate Education (RUE) program is a small, highly competitive route for applicants whose education was delayed or interrupted. The published guidelines generally require being at least six years beyond high school, no prior bachelor’s degree, and no more than roughly two years of full-time college study. The Brown-specific RUE application opens October 1; the current pages show a March 2 application deadline, while one requirements page still references March 1, so the live portal must control. The more important routing fact for this applicant is that Brown instructs U.S. veterans and current service members to use the Brown Veterans Application regardless of high-school year or accumulated college credit—not RUE or the Common App. The Veterans Application opens in August, has a March 1 final deadline, and is reviewed on a rolling basis. Brown’s 2024–25 CDS reports 2,987 Fall 2024 conventional transfer applicants, 215 admits, and 145 enrollees, a 7.2% rate; it does not isolate RUE or Veterans Application outcomes, so it is not a program-specific probability.

Brown’s CDS marks level of applicant interest Not Considered for first-year admission, and Brown publishes no transfer interest score. Visits, emails, and events should be used to decide whether Brown’s Open Curriculum and credit structure actually fit, not to produce telemetry. A substantive question is: “For a Veterans Application entrant with SCAD Applied AI studio and computing courses, how have project-based courses typically mapped into Brown course credit, and what sequencing would remain for computer science, Science/Technology/Society, or Modern Culture and Media study?” Brown accepts electronically supplied materials and portal submissions; a mailed newsletter or creative package is not an admissions credential. The Veterans Application does have a distinctive rolling binding option: if admitted under that option, the applicant must enroll and withdraw other applications. It is not standard transfer ED and Brown does not publish a causal admissions boost. Use it only if Brown is unequivocally first choice and the financial-aid estimate is acceptable, because it eliminates the ability to compare later offers.

Brown’s Open Curriculum can support a tailored combination of computer science or data science with Science, Technology, and Society, Modern Culture and Media, sociology, or visual inquiry. Suresh Venkatasubramanian, a professor of computer science and data science and director of Brown’s Center for Technological Responsibility, Reimagination and Redesign (CNTR), studies algorithmic fairness and the societal governance of technology. Harini Suresh, an assistant professor of computer science, studies the sociotechnical dimensions of AI, including fairness and how affected communities experience automated systems. CNTR’s socially responsible computing work provides a concrete bridge from SCAD’s applied design training to liberal-arts questions about who defines a system’s goals, whose evidence counts, and how harm is measured. The application should make that bridge through a finished project and a specific unresolved question, not merely list faculty names. Brown’s optional 90-second video can add voice and presence, but should not duplicate the résumé or essay.

Brown is a Service to School VetLink partner and its Veterans Application is need-blind for U.S. veterans; Brown states that it meets full demonstrated need and offers an unlimited undergraduate Yellow Ribbon program for eligible students. Recommendations are flexible but evidence-based: for an applicant with recent college work, at least one academic letter is preferred, while a commanding officer, supervisor, civilian employer, or community leader can supply a second perspective. Brown also welcomes the JST, résumé, optional video, and Service to School VetLink Addendum. Summer/fall priorities are therefore to complete the Service to School intake, obtain the VetLink Addendum if eligible, decide between rolling binding and nonbinding review only after cost analysis, and produce a coherent transfer-credit and academic plan. After applying, use the portal, respond to any aid requests, and send concise material updates; do not cultivate a one-month alumnus or faculty acquaintance as a pseudo-recommender.

Brown’s Socially Responsible Computing program is an implemented curricular initiative rather than a stand-alone ethics slogan. Since 2019, specially trained Socially Responsible Computing teaching assistants have worked inside technical courses to connect algorithms and systems to their social and political consequences. CNTR and the CS program also built a public handbook that turns interdisciplinary material into teachable primers and resources; the 2025–26 project teams included undergraduates in computer science, behavioral decision sciences, public policy, illustration, graphic design, philosophy, and STS, working on AI, privacy, accessibility, product design, and development. This matters because it shows exactly how a design-and-AI transfer could contribute: not by cold-emailing the director, but by bringing visual communication and user research into a documented, cross-disciplinary curriculum project after enrollment.
actions: Use the Brown Veterans Application, as Brown explicitly directs veterans to do; do not submit RUE or the Common App in parallel.
Complete Service to School/VetLink early enough to develop the addendum and application strategy before Brown’s August opening.
Request an academic recommendation now and a service/professional recommendation from someone with direct, sustained knowledge.
Compare binding and nonbinding Veterans Application review only after running Brown’s aid estimate and understanding the withdrawal obligation.
Map SCAD syllabi to Brown’s course-credit system and use the credit question above if the public guidance cannot resolve the ambiguity.
Complete the optional video if it adds character and reflection; do not turn it into an advertisement or repeat the written application.

Ordinary Common App transfers may put an online-presence link in Brown Activities, but that instruction should not be assumed to create a field in the Veterans Application.
brown.safest: Use the Veterans Application. Put one kendren.us case-study link (and a clean GitHub link only if useful) in the approved résumé, then use the strongly encouraged 90-second video and VetLink Addendum to explain the human problem, method, result, and lesson. Do not rely on the ordinary-transfer Activities field.

princeton.title: Princeton University
paras: Princeton’s transfer process has one fall-entry cycle. The official calendar lists March 1 for the Common Application, Princeton-specific questions, required graded written paper, transcripts, College Report, and recommendations; the optional Arts Supplement and financial-aid application are due March 9, submitted tests should arrive by the end of March, decisions are released in mid-May, and the reply deadline is in late May. Princeton requires two academic recommendations, at least one from a college instructor, and places unusual value on the graded paper as direct evidence of college-level reasoning and writing. Its 2025–26 CDS reports 2,274 Fall 2025 transfer applicants, 42 admits, and 32 enrollees, a 1.85% admit rate. Princeton also reports that 22 of the 32 enrolled Fall 2025 transfers had served in the military and 27 came from community colleges, which confirms that veteran/nontraditional recruitment is real but not easy. There is no transfer ED, ED II, or Single-Choice Early Action plan; those early concepts do not apply to this March transfer cycle.

Princeton says explicitly that it does not track demonstrated interest and that attending an information session does not affect admission. The correct strategy is to use events to improve the application, never as a points system. A useful transfer question is: “How are SCAD Applied AI and studio courses evaluated toward Princeton distribution, departmental prerequisites, and elective credit, and what kind of graded paper best demonstrates readiness when most recent work combines design and technical production?” The first half belongs with transfer/advising staff; the second can be asked in an official transfer session if not covered publicly. Do not send physical portfolios outside the optional Arts Supplement, mass-email professors, ask an alumnus for an endorsement, or use automated email interaction. Those acts do not overcome the central evidence Princeton requests: recent academic excellence, rigorous writing, recommendations, service and leadership context, and a compelling reason that Princeton’s curriculum is necessary.

The likely academic home is the AB in Computer Science paired with the Computing, Society and Policy minor, Technology and Society minor, visual arts, sociology, or African American studies. Olga Russakovsky leads work in computer vision, human-centered AI, and fairness/accountability through the Visual AI Lab. Arvind Narayanan, director of the Center for Information Technology Policy, studies the societal impact and evaluation of AI, privacy, and de-identification. Ruha Benjamin, the Alexander Stewart 1886 Professor of African American Studies, studies science, technology, and social inequity. Together these resources support a high-level narrative: SCAD developed the applicant’s ability to make AI-mediated experiences, while Princeton would supply theoretical computer science, policy, sociology, and critical methods to test who benefits from those experiences. The graded paper should be the strongest instructor-evaluated analytical work available—not a newly manufactured essay—and the application should show intellectual continuity between it and the proposed Princeton work.

Princeton actively recruits military applicants, offers an application-fee waiver, participates in Service to School VetLink, Warrior-Scholar Project, and the Leadership Scholar Program, and provides a dedicated transfer/veteran community. It is need-blind for U.S. applicants and meets demonstrated need with grants; eligible veterans can also coordinate Yellow Ribbon/VA benefits. Alex Bustin is the named military-admissions contact, Silvia Rodriguez is the veteran financial-aid contact, and Keith Shaw directs the transfer and veteran program. Summer/fall priorities are to complete S2S/VetLink and, if appropriate, a Warrior-Scholar academic boot camp; earn current rigorous grades; secure the graded paper with its instructor’s comments and grade; ask two credible academic recommenders; and prepare an exact credit and academic plan. After applying, complete aid by March 9, monitor the portal, and report material achievements only. Princeton’s current policy remains test optional for Fall 2027 entry, with testing scheduled to return for Fall 2028; active-duty military applicants are exempt under the announced return policy.

A concrete Princeton research asset is H-ARC, a public behavioral dataset created to compare human abstraction and reasoning with AI systems. Researchers collected solution attempts from more than 1,700 people across all 400 training and 400 evaluation tasks in the original Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus, publishing not only final answers but step-by-step action traces and natural-language descriptions of the rules participants inferred. It is the largest human evaluation of ARC reported by the project and matters because it lets researchers study how people form abstractions instead of judging intelligence from accuracy alone. For this applicant, H-ARC is a model for combining interface design, cognitive science, data documentation, and AI evaluation in one reproducible project.
actions: Choose the graded paper now and preserve the instructor’s grade/comments; ask Princeton if a mixed design/technical course paper fits only if the published rule is ambiguous.
Establish two academic recommenders, including at least one college instructor, before fall workload intensifies.
Complete Service to School/VetLink and explore Warrior-Scholar Project or Leadership Scholar Program on their actual eligibility and timing.
Build the academic case around a specific link among Computer Science, CITP, visual practice, and social analysis.
Prepare every required item for March 1 and the Arts Supplement/aid items for March 9; do not rely on postal extras.
Treat the 1.85% institutional rate as a reach baseline and maintain financially and academically sound alternatives.
