uga.title: University of Georgia
paras: UGA’s Athens-campus Summer/Fall transfer application currently opens January 22 and has a March 1 application-and-materials deadline, with most decisions in mid-to-late March. Fall 2027 dates have not yet been posted, so use those as working dates and reconfirm in January. Applicants with fewer than 30 completed transferable semester hours by the deadline are ineligible. Those with 30–59 hours generally need a calculated transfer GPA of at least 3.30 plus the time-since-high-school conditions listed by UGA; applicants with 60 or more hours generally need at least a 3.00. High-demand majors can require a second application after admission.

UGA is more transcript- and threshold-driven than interest-driven. Its 2024–25 CDS reports 3,099 transfer applicants, 2,471 admits, and 1,852 enrollees, about 79.7%; a newer official 2025 transfer update described roughly 3,800 applications and about 2,460 admits, around 64.7%, with an admitted average GPA of 3.71. The year-to-year change shows why one historical rate is not a guarantee. UGA also calculates its own transfer GPA and only reviews completed work received by the deadline; in-progress spring work after March 1 may not rescue an otherwise ineligible file. The highest-value summer task is therefore a precise credit/GPA audit, not admissions outreach.

Academically, UGA’s Institute for Artificial Intelligence is unusually interdisciplinary, joining computing with philosophy, psychology, linguistics, engineering, agriculture, and other fields. Prashant Doshi, UGA Foundation Distinguished Professor of Artificial Intelligence and the Institute’s Executive Director, works on multi-agent decision-making and human-robot collaboration, including customizable autonomy and agricultural cobots. Kyle Johnsen, Professor of Electrical and Computer Engineering and the Institute’s Associate Director for Research and Outreach, works in immersive and interactive systems. A liberal-arts proposal could connect SCAD’s agentic and human-in-the-loop design to cognitive science, philosophy, sociology, or linguistics while continuing applied prototyping.

Your useful questions are administrative and curricular: which SCAD quarter courses UGA has deemed transferable, how quarter hours are converted for the 30/60-hour thresholds, and whether the intended major is high demand. The Institute and School of Computing post colloquia, including public AI-for-social-good talks; those can be free learning opportunities. Do not ask an Institute director to help you get admitted or to write a quick recommendation. If you develop a sustained, evaluated project through a formal workshop, course, or research collaboration, that supervisor may later be a legitimate supplemental recommender where allowed—but a one-month correspondence relationship is not equivalent to an academic recommendation.

uchicago.title: University of Chicago
paras: UChicago is one of only two schools in this list with a conventional, expressly named binding Transfer Early Decision option; Brown's separate Veterans Application also offers a distinct rolling binding choice. UChicago's page still displays the prior cycle: TED was due March 2, 2026 because March 1 fell on a weekend, with a late-March decision; Transfer Rolling used the same opening deadline and continued to June 1. The stated rule is 11:59 p.m. on March 1 or the first business day of March. Use March 1, 2027 as the working TED deadline, then verify when the 2027 transfer page updates. TED requires a signed agreement and withdrawal of other applications if admitted. It is appropriate only after a full credit, curriculum, cost, and benefits review.

The 2024–25 UChicago CDS reports 2,884 transfer applicants, 268 admits, and 231 enrollees, an overall transfer admit rate of about 9.3%. UChicago does not publish the TED applicant or admit count, so there is no defensible TED acceptance rate and no way to convert “binding” into personal odds. Its transfer review is also need-aware, although the university says it will meet 100% of demonstrated need with a loan-free package for admitted transfers who applied for aid. TED is a meaningful commitment signal, not a substitute for readiness. UChicago requires two teacher evaluations, a college report and midterm report where applicable, high-school and college transcripts, and its supplement; it recommends a short video and permits relevant optional supplements.

The intellectual match could be excellent if you want to convert SCAD’s design-and-build foundation into computational social science, sociology of knowledge, ethics, or human-centered computing. James A. Evans, Max Palevsky Professor of Sociology and director of Knowledge Lab, studies how knowledge and innovation emerge using machine learning, networks, crowdsourcing, and computational social science. UChicago’s computer-science community also includes human-centered and responsible-computing work; Ben Y. Zhao studies security and adversarial effects around AI, while HCI faculty and the Media Arts, Data, and Design ecosystem connect computation to creative practice. The strongest essay would explain why the Core and social-science theory are necessary to test the assumptions embedded in your local-AI systems.

Contact the transfer office only after solving what the website can solve. A worthwhile question is how a veteran or long-removed student should balance the two academic recommendations when one recent instructor can assess classroom work and a commanding officer can assess disciplined inquiry; UChicago explicitly allows a supervisor, mentor, or commanding officer when an applicant has been out of school for a significant period. Another is how many SCAD quarter credits are likely to remain usable given UChicago’s six-quarter residency and Core rules. Attend free Knowledge Lab or Data Science Institute talks and let them sharpen your research. Do not bind TED until the net price, GI Bill/Yellow Ribbon treatment, family obligations, and likely credit loss are acceptable.

nu.title: Northwestern University
paras: Northwestern is the second school on this list with a conventional, expressly named binding Transfer Early Decision plan; Brown's veteran-specific binding choice is a separate route. Northwestern's Fall 2027 dates are already posted: TED is due March 1, 2027 with a decision in early April; Regular Decision is due April 1 with decisions in mid-to-late May. Financial-aid materials share the application deadline. Northwestern requires all secondary and college transcripts, a college report, one academic evaluation, the transfer writing supplements, and an ED agreement for TED; tests are optional. The university says the financial-aid offer is calculated the same way in TED and RD, but admission for transfer applicants considers financial need.

The 2024–25 Northwestern CDS reports 4,045 transfer applicants, 484 admits, and 277 enrollees, an overall admit rate of about 12.0%. TED is new for this cycle, so there is no historical TED admit rate. Northwestern says it expects a higher TED acceptance rate because of interest, anticipated pool strength, and alignment, but that is not a numerical promise and partly reflects applicant selection. Your personal likelihood cannot be responsibly estimated without college GPA, completed credits, high-school record, veteran/service history, prerequisites, intended Northwestern school, aid need, and the quality of your transfer reason. Treat 12.0% as an old overall baseline and TED as a commitment option—not as a mathematical shortcut.

Northwestern offers one of the most direct design-to-liberal-arts bridges in the group. Elizabeth Gerber, Professor of Mechanical Engineering, Communication Studies, and by courtesy Computer Science, co-directs the Center for Human-Computer Interaction + Design and teaches human-centered product/service design and Designing with AI; her work studies collective innovation and sociotechnical systems. Nicholas Diakopoulos, Professor of Communication Studies and Computer Science by courtesy, directs the Computational Journalism Lab and studies algorithmic accountability, transparency, automation, and news. The HCI+D Center also links design, learning sciences, communication, computing, psychology, and social behavior. That is a credible continuation of SCAD contextual research, collaboration, ethics, agentic design, and human-in-the-loop work.

The best transfer-office question is school-specific: “If I apply to Weinberg for a liberal-arts major, what access do undergraduates realistically have to HCI+D, Segal Design, communication, and computer-science courses, and which cross-school pathway should I cite accurately?” Another asks how SCAD quarter credits and studio courses affect class standing and time-to-degree. HCI+D runs public and virtual Thought Leader Dialogues and maintains a listserv; follow it for free intellectual programming, not application telemetry. Do not cold-email Gerber or Diakopoulos for an admissions recommendation. If Northwestern is genuinely the first choice after aid and credit analysis, TED is the strongest legitimate interest signal available; if not, use RD without apology.

brown.diText: Brown publishes no transfer interest score. The binding rolling option is a contractual commitment, not a signal.
brown.path: A policy-oriented concentration, Africana Studies, Science, Technology and Society, or Modern Culture and Media. Not computer science first. On your call Brown noted that a concentration is like a major with its own requirements, and that even a policy concentration can carry a math requirement, so statistics helps. Confirm the exact concentration.
know: Suresh Venkatasubramanian
Directs the Center for Technological Responsibility, Reimagination and Redesign (CNTR): technology and policy lane.
Harini Suresh
Sociotechnical dimensions of AI, fairness and how affected communities experience automated systems.
brown.res: CNTR and the Socially Responsible Computing program
brown.evi: Since 2019, trained Socially Responsible Computing teaching assistants work inside technical courses. CNTR and the CS program built a public handbook of teachable primers, and the 2025-26 teams spanned CS, public policy, graphic design, philosophy and STS.
brown.who: Becky (Veterans admissions, call held). Brown is a Service to School VetLink partner.
brown.ask: How have project-based courses typically mapped into Brown credit, and what sequencing would remain for a policy, Africana Studies or STS concentration?
brown.show: One finished project plus one unresolved question. Use the optional 90-second video for voice, not a résumé recap. Include the JST, résumé and VetLink Addendum.
brown.dont: Do not submit the Common App or RUE in parallel. Do not cold-email the CNTR director.

cornell.diText: Cornell publishes no transfer interest factor. Choosing the right college and finishing its prerequisites matter far more.
cornell.path: ILR BS: labor, technology, workplace systems, policy and economics. Africana Studies is available as a minor, and as a transfer you cannot double major across two Cornell colleges (Kyle, call). The earlier faculty research was written for Information Science, so treat it as method context until ILR faculty are researched.
know: Claire Cardie
Natural-language processing, argumentation and human-centered NLP.
Allison Koenecke
Algorithmic fairness, including automated systems in public benefits and health.
René Kizilcec
Directs the Future of Learning Lab; education technology and computational social science.
cornell.evi: A field study of 1.4 million registrations across 159 online courses at 20 institutions found that course discipline, stated prerequisites and gender cues predicted who enrolled, while instructor skin color, diversity references and description style did not show the expected effects.
cornell.who: Kyle (admissions, call held), ILR transfer admissions, and the Cornell veterans admissions ambassador.
cornell.ask: Please evaluate these exact course titles, descriptions and grades for ILR sophomore or junior entry.
cornell.show: One finished project with its human consequences, tied to a specific Cornell method. The required recommendation comes from a college instructor who graded substantial work.
cornell.dont: Do not mass-contact faculty or mail packages. Name a professor only after reading one current project or paper.

nd.diText: Notre Dame says it does not track prospective-student interest. What counts is prerequisites at B or higher, college performance, a specific transfer statement and space in the major.
nd.path: College of Arts and Letters with Africana Studies as the likely major, plus the cross-college Tech Ethics minor. Law school is the long-term aim, and the veterans law clinic came up on your call. The IDEA Center is a resource, not a degree.
know: Mohammad Rashidujjaman Rifat
HCI; AI ethics and cultural and value pluralism.
Nitesh Chawla
Founding director of the Lucy Family Institute for Data and Society.
Meghan Sullivan
Director of the Institute for Ethics and the Common Good.
nd.evi: The BenchmarkCards project standardized documentation of LLM benchmark properties, bias and evaluation methods, with a public benchmark database. The Ethical Cities program pairs students and faculty with South Bend organizations.
nd.who: Montanna Kirven (veteran liaison) or the Office of Military and Veterans Affairs. Michael (call held).
nd.ask: How will the 24-credit threshold and Arts and Letters prerequisites treat my quarter-based SCAD Applied AI studios?
nd.show: A PDF syllabus for every post-high-school course, named exactly by course number. A transfer statement built on technology ethics and the common good. The optional 60 to 90 second Glimpse video only if it adds voice.
nd.dont: Do not ask the liaison, a professor or an alumnus for a recommendation. Do not mail extras.

yale.diText: Yale states that it does not track event registration or contact with admissions staff.

Human-robot interaction and social AI.
Theodore Kim
Computer graphics and the Critical Computing Initiative.
